title: Inkwell — Oncall Notebook (overnight handoff)
content:
INKWELL ONCALL — overnight handoff (scratchpad)

Quick context:
- Shift owner: Maya R. Chen (tonight) — taking notes for next shift.
- Short summary: intermittent latency spikes on hosted-api region-us-east-1 starting ~02:10 UTC; suspected KV-cache churn after autoscale event. No customer-facing errors observed yet (5xx rate stable), but p95 token latency spiked to ~2.4s for a short window.

What I saw (timeline):
- 01:58 UTC: autoscaler triggered additional serving pods for model-12b-quant due to a burst from load-test suite (tests on dev tenant).
- 02:06 UTC: dashboard shows small but sharp increase in cache miss ratio on kv-cache-1 (prefix cache eviction count +120 in 3m).
- 02:10 UTC: alert SRE-4129 fired (p95-token-latency > 1.8s for >5m).
- 02:14 UTC: p95 recovered to baseline after cache warmed; alert auto-resolved.
- 03:02 UTC: another small spike coinciding with a canary rollout (see linked PR).

Current alerts/monitors (as of last check 03:30 UTC):
- p95-token-latency: OK (0.78s)
- kv-cache-miss-rate: elevated but falling (0.12 -> 0.05 over 30m)
- model-serving-errors-5xx: OK (0.02%)
- node-cpu-utilization: OK

Ongoing issues to track:
- KV cache eviction pattern when pods scale up quickly. Root cause unknown: eviction threshold tuning or cold-start warmup behavior.
- Canary rollout PR 874 may interact with cache warming logic (linked).

Quick triage checklist (for next shift):
1) Check recent autoscale events: rwi infra autoscale events --since 6h | grep model-12b-quant
2) Inspect kv-cache metrics: open dashboard 'kv-cache-overview' -> check 'evictions', 'hit-rate' by pod.
3) If p95 > 1.5s for >10m: escalate to SRE oncall lead (Alex Kim) and pause canary via rollout control.
4) If 5xx > 0.5% sustained: open P0 incident and notify eng-serving-runtime.

Useful commands (shorthand):
- Get pods for serving group: kubectl get pods -n serving -l model=model-12b-quant -o wide
- Tail logs for a pod: kubectl logs -n serving <pod> -c runtime --since=10m | grep -i "evict"
- Query cache stats (internal CLI): rwi runtime cache-stats --cluster us-east-1 --pool kv-cache-1
- Rollback canary: rwi rollout pause --service hosted-api --canary-id=<id>

Temporary mitigations attempted tonight:
- Added a short-lived cache-warmup job for new pods (manual run) -> observed immediate hit-rate improvement for that pod group.
- Increased cache size for kv-cache-1 by +10% via emergency flag (monitoring only, will revert if no benefit after 24h).

Escalation contacts (order):
1) Alex Kim (SRE lead) — slack @alex.k (pager if >15m)
2) Diego Morales (serving-runtime) — slack @diego (call if 5xx spike)
3) Priya Singh (product-hosted-api) — for customer impact and communication

Notes to next shift (do this first):
- Check if cache size revert happened (I left revert scheduled for 26-03-11 02:00 UTC - cancel if still needed).
- Confirm whether dev-team load-tests were re-scheduled; if so, coordinate to avoid triggering autoscale. Ticket: DEVOPS-2291.
- If you see repeated p95 spikes after warmup, set temporary traffic route to model-7b-quant via smart routing policy: rwi routing set-fallback --from model-12b-quant --to model-7b-quant --threshold 1.2s

Open questions / TODOs:
- Why did KV evictions spike only for model-12b-quant pods and not for others on same node? (Investigate memory allocation per process and kernel OOM adj.)
- Is the cache eviction algorithm honoring pinned keys for long-lived sessions? (Ping runtime team; see PR 874 comments.)
- Add an automated warmup hook in the autoscaler for serving pods (proposal in draft, link in linked_artifacts).

Ad-hoc observations and heuristics (notes to self):
- Warmup job (curl /warmup endpoint 10x) seems to reduce first-minute latency by ~30% in my quick tests. Might be useful as a stop-gap.
- If you need to test without impacting customers: use the 'dev-load' tenant (tenant id dev-load) and run load in staging region.

Last shift artifacts / breadcrumbs:
- Pull logs exported to /tmp/inkwell-logs-20260310.tar.gz (on my jump host) — contains cache-stats and autoscale events.
- Slack thread: #sre-nightwatch thread 'kv-cache spikes' (pin for context).

Sign-off to next:
- Leaving the cache size +10% until 2026-03-11 02:00 UTC; if you don't see regressions, leave or adjust as needed.
- General ask: please document any manual rollbacks or temporary flags you use in this doc (append timestamp + short note).

-- Maya

Notes to self (private scratch):
- If I get pulled into paging further, remember to add root cause note under 'linked_artifacts' after ticket created.
- Follow up with runtime team about whether PR 874 should include a warmup hook.
